title: Two customer names that differ only in capitals keep one order everywhere
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Two of your customers with open invoices have names that differ only in capital letters.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two customers have open invoices on today's date and their names differ only in capitals: {Customer-A} and {Customer-B}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-05 Ace Towing and {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-05 ACE TOWING.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Find {Customer-A} and {Customer-B} in the list and note which one is higher.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu at the right of the title.
  3. Open the PDF and find the two names.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet program and find the two names.
  6. Reload the page and find the two names again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the two customers sit next to each other (no other customer between them) in one order.
  • Step 2: the PDF downloads.
  • Step 3: the two names are in the same order as on screen.
  • Step 4: the CSV downloads.
  • Step 5: the two rows are in the same order as on screen.
  • Step 6: after the reload they are still in the same order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • S1-R4: “Two names that compare equal are ordered by the plain lower-cased name, then by the customer or vendor itself, so the same two customers always come out in the same order on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV. For example, "Emile's Towing" comes before "Émile's Towing": the accent folds for the name order (S1-R3), so the two tie, and in the plain lower-cased name the unaccented letter comes first.”
  • S1-R2: “Name order compares names ignoring capitals, in plain character order: digits and punctuation compare as characters, so "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" and "A-1 Towing" before "a1 towing". Names that start with a punctuation mark follow the same order: "#1 Diesel", "-1 Diesel", "10 Trucking", "@Home Towing".”
  • S3-R2: “The PDF downloads as a file.”
